answer: Make holding many keys a liability. Each identity locks a bond. Anyone who posts a message co-signed by two identities, a bridge proving one party holds both private keys, collects half of both bonds and the rest burns. Independent agents never hold each other's keys, so they risk nothing. A farm keeps hundreds of keys on one server; one leaked backup or bribed contractor can turn its velvet-lined vault into a tide of claims, draining every bond at once. Farmers must then trust every insider forever. (Split and bond size illustrative; bonds must be large enough to tempt.)
